items.title: The functor of points where a module is flat in dimensions at least n is unchanged by etale localisation on the source when the etale image contains the relative associated points
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter flat.tex (More on Flatness), section 'The local structure of a finite type module'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file flat.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: Inside the flatness-in-dimension-n setup, the lemma compares the functor F_n attached to (f : X -> S, F) with the functor F'_n attached to the etale base change h : X' -> X: F_n is always a subfunctor of F'_n, and the two agree as soon as h(X') contains the relative associated points of F over S (statement lines 7727-7736). The first part of the proof is a dimension comparison: after an arbitrary base change T -> S the non-flatness loci Z in the fibre X_t and Z' in X'_t satisfy Z' = h_t^{-1}(Z) by flatness permanence along the etale h_T, so Z' -> Z is etale and dim(Z') <= dim(Z), which gives F_n inside F'_n (proof lines 7739-7751). The converse is where the associated-points hypothesis is used: assuming F'_n(T) nonempty and a component of Z of dimension at least n, the author picks a generic point xi of that component and a generalisation x of xi that is an associated point of F_t, uses the relative associated points base change lemmas to place x in the image of h_T, and concludes from x not in Z' and flatness permanence that F_T is flat at x, which by the flatness-checking theorem contradicts dim(Z) >= n (proof lines 7753-7774). Locating the generalisation of xi in the image of h_T and turning flatness at x into flatness at xi is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
